candidates.title: Daily job alerts for target companies

demandEvidence.chore: Track target-company job postings and send an alert when new postings appear.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Workflow: Schedule Trigger (daily) → Apify node (“Run an Actor and get dataset”) → IF item count > 0 → Slack.

ease.reason: The supplied post shows a daily scheduled scraper-to-Slack loop; setup and actor availability still need validation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: recruiting consultants or job-search services might pay for monitored alerts; no buyer or payment is established.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can track a small supplied company list; source coverage and actor costs vary and need operator checks.

autonomy.reason: The post describes daily retrieval and notification; a person must choose targets and verify listings, and the node reference supports only counts.

evidence.reason: The native spans show a daily job-scraping alert and remembered seen jobs; the reference documents count and unique count only.

experimentPlan.output: A daily digest of newly observed postings for a short operator-supplied company list.
inputs: A short list of company career pages or supported job sources
A small set of fictional or public sample job records
experimentPlan.trigger: At a daily scheduled run, process the selected sources and prepare a digest only when new matching records appear.
steps: Load the selected company and role filters.
Retrieve the supported sample or configured source records.
Compare records with a saved seen-item list.
Count and group new records for a digest.
Send the draft digest to an operator for review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On repeated sample inputs, previously seen records are not shown again, and each new record appears once with its source URL.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator must select permitted sources, check listing accuracy, control any paid actor usage, and approve recipients; no automated applications are proposed.
unverified: Supported source coverage beyond the described actors is unknown.
The supplied Summarize documentation supports counts, not deduplication or scheduling.
Delivery reliability, operating cost and customer willingness to pay are unverified.

candidates.reason: Concrete daily alert workflow, but a limited documented building reference and unproven buyer make its provisional mean below six.

candidates.title: Prepare answers for repeated application fields

demandEvidence.chore: Repeatedly enter resume information into newly developed forms for one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

ease.reason: A beginner can test sample resume text against a manually supplied field list; n8n documents structured extraction from text, not employer-form reading.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers or career-support services might pay for answer preparation; this post shows a chore, not purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week review-sheet prototype is bounded; the Information Extractor supports schema-based text extraction but not browser automation or form submission.

autonomy.reason: Structured extraction can suggest fields, but a person must check every answer and manually complete each employer form.

evidence.reason: The post reports daily resume entry into company-specific forms; n8n documentation supports structured extraction only, with no workflow or buyer corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet that maps supplied resume facts to draft answers for repeated job-application fields.
inputs: Fictional resume facts supplied by the tester
A small set of manually transcribed sample form field labels
experimentPlan.trigger: When a tester receives another application form with fields represented in the sample set.
steps: Enter fictional resume facts into a structured table.
Add the sample form field labels.
Use the documented Information Extractor with a declared output schema to suggest matching facts.
Flag fields with no clear match instead of guessing.
Have a person review and copy approved answers manually.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each sample field, verify the suggested answer matches the corresponding fictional resume fact and leaves uncertain fields blank.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must provide lawful test inputs, check every answer, handle sensitive information safely, and complete the actual application.
unverified: Actual employer form layouts and field variations are unavailable.
No supplied source supports browser automation or automatic submission.
Whether job seekers or career services would pay is unknown.

candidates.reason: The refreshed chore and structured-extraction reference support a bounded review-sheet experiment; provisional mean remains below six.

candidates.title: Draft recovery checks for AI agent workflows

demandEvidence.chore: Developers must write checkpointing and recovery logic and handle idempotency for agents.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

ease.reason: A student can draft a checklist from operator-supplied scenarios, but no supplied reference documents checkpoint or idempotency behavior.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agents may pay for recovery setup help; the post states a problem without purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic scenario checklist is possible, while safe retry semantics depend on each agent and external side effects.

autonomy.reason: The proposed output is a human-reviewed design checklist; no automated recovery capability is documented and an engineer must authorize retries.

evidence.reason: The excerpt identifies checkpointers, recovery logic and idempotency work, but gives no concrete failure scenario, inputs or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A review checklist for retry and checkpoint decisions in one fictional agent workflow.
inputs: A set of synthetic failure and retry scenarios
experimentPlan.trigger: When a developer supplies a proposed workflow and wants to review its recovery cases.
steps: List each step and any external side effect.
Mark the proposed checkpoint location for each step.
Describe synthetic failures before and after each checkpoint.
Flag retries that could repeat an external side effect.
Ask an engineer to review and approve any recovery design.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each synthetic scenario, check that the checklist identifies whether retrying could repeat a side effect and leaves unresolved cases flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An engineer must supply the workflow, define safe idempotency behavior, and approve all production changes; no recovery code execution is proposed.
unverified: No supplied reference supports checkpointing or idempotency mechanics.
Safe retry rules depend on workflow-specific side effects.
Buyer willingness to pay and frequency are unknown.

candidates.reason: The excerpt identifies a real engineering burden but lacks scenario detail or implementation support; a synthetic checklist is below threshold.
